name: McNeave Nally
role: Former Medora resident; witness in the Luffsey murder case
bio: McNeave Nally was to run a mercantile business at Medora for Mr. Huggins in 1884 and later moved to Jamestown. In September 1885 he returned as a witness in the Luffsey murder case, testifying that he had served on the coroner's jury, and in July 1886 the paper reported the death of his father in County Mayo, Ireland.

moments.label: Testified about the coroner's jury in the Luffsey case

mentions: …and, has made up his mind to stay with us and go into business. He will go into some mercantile business with McNeave Nally in charge, and besides will go into the business of raising horses. He cannot possibly find a better location for both. The growth Medora is bound to undergo will…
…loss. He is too much of a rustler, however, to be discouraged, and is already on the alert for work. He left McNeave Nally in Jamestown, and brought back Jack Cameron in charge of his outfit.
McNeave Nally, now in Jimtown, has joined the fold and added his name to the Cow Boy list. He sends regards to all his old friends here.
McNeavo Nally, a former resident of Medora, now at Jamestown, came in Sunday. He is a witness in the Luffsey murder case and accompanied surveyor Heinze here.

…and tramped down. Paul Heinze exhibited a sketch of the scene, showing the relative positions of the parties. McNeave Nally testified that he was on the coroner's jury and described the wound which caused Luffsey's death.
